title: Censorship on Youtube: How Greg Doucette betrayed the entire Fitness community
summary: A long rant against Greg Doucette after he copyright-struck Geoffrey Verity Schofield's critical video, framed around free speech, abuse of power by big channels, and fanboy raids. He also criticizes Greg's overpriced cookbook and plans, his debate tactics toward Team3DAlpha and others, and his marketing to novices, while granting that Greg still gives some good advice and was right about maingaining.
claims: He refuses to make drama videos to grow his channel and only goes after people he considers actively dangerous
Copyright striking a critic's fair-use video under false pretenses is the one line he cannot forgive, and Greg crossed it with Geoffrey Verity Schofield
He previously agreed with Greg that maingaining works and that novices do not need absurd bulks to gain muscle
Fanboy culture makes people swing from total love to total hate; Greg did wrong but still gives good advice
Free speech is absolute; the legal system favors whoever can afford lawyers, which is why strikes by powerful channels are abusive
Team3DAlpha made a video on myonuclear overload, a valid hypertrophy concept, and Greg answered with a strawman, ignored the rebuttal, and his audience raided the channel
Greg's pattern with critics: twist their words, ignore solid rebuttals, and finally censor
Greg put screenshots of NH's comments in a video without the context of his replies, which led Greg's audience to attack him in the comments
You judge a person by how they treat those below them; Greg goes easy on big names like PewDiePie but crushes small channels
Calling critics mosquitoes dehumanizes them and teaches fans to treat free thinkers like animals
Athlean-X used fake weights to market strength programs to novices and survived through censorship because he is too big to fail
A $100 training ebook and Greg's cookbook are heavily overpriced; the parasocial bond with his audience is what lets him charge that
Fitness knowledge is free; selling expensive plans is like selling $25 bottles of water at a festival where free water is available in a hidden spot
A grossly overweight novice will lose weight on almost any diet and exercise, so his transformation does not prove a coach's program
$1000 for plans is overpriced, and saying no price is too high for health is fearmongering
In his opinion a program should be made by you yourself
Greg demotivates natural lifters with very low natural standards and lacks knowledge of RP, training to failure and programming
Many big fitness pages sell regurgitated template plans as custom programs
Striking a video at 20K views within 24 hours kills its algorithmic momentum even if it is later restored
He has received death threats for criticizing Greg, which he blames on Greg's behavior
He followed Greg for about seven years, says his channel of roughly 10,000 subs is not monetized, and will unsubscribe and stop commenting until Greg apologizes
